answer: The basalt exchange denies earning access unless each key sustains 10 Mbps of independently metered upload for 1 hour, so every extra alias requires another concurrent 10 Mbps. Receivers issue different unpredictable streams and reject shared receipts; a single uplink must divide its finite capacity, not count it twice. The shale and karst desks share meter records. This bandwidth rule depends on honest receivers and useful traffic; cheap transit providers retain an advantage.
